items.title: 56422_Leonard Phillips oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee narrates the history of Ben Webster's relationship with Lester Young ('Mr. Young taught Ben how to play saxophone') and mentions Ben Webster in the context of Jap Allen's band, but does not describe a direct personal interaction or professional relationship between himself (Leonard P

ctx.x: That's when guys started playing tenors. Ben Webster. Mr. Young taught Ben how to play saxophone. Ben was a piano player. He was playing and violin. Ben said, "I used to hear ole Les in the room, man, playin' that horn, and I'd get in there and try to run over and play, but that cat was gone." But Ben learned fast, you know. He was fooling with alto first, and then he got on tenor, but in a... He stayed with Mr. Young I guess about a year playing piano, and then he was practicing on the saxophone at the same…
He was kind of into Hawkins, wasn't he?
